root_cause: The loop exit logic in Curl_get_line only checks feof(input) (via `*eof`) to decide when to stop retrying fgets(); it never checks ferror(input), so a persistent I/O error (which makes fgets() keep returning NULL while feof() stays false) is indistinguishable from 'just keep reading' and the loop never terminates.
findings: Curl_get_line() reads a config/cache/cookie/hsts/netrc file line by line using fgets() in a 'while(1)' loop. The rewritten loop sets `*eof = feof(input);` right after the fgets() call and only breaks out of the loop (returning) when `*eof` becomes true (real EOF) or a full line terminated by '\n' has been accumulated.
